title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Vectora Systems)
summary: Intro discovery focused on open model selection and deployment mode tradeoffs. Customer needs: multilingual support, long context for document understanding (32k+), tool-calling for internal search and DB lookups, and options for Private deployment due to data residency. Agreed next steps: send pricing/benchmark plan, security pack, and schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
action_items: Alex Moreno - send Hosted/Dedicated/Private pricing and model cost projection - due 2027-12-08
Priya Shah - propose benchmark test plan (latency/throughput/quality) and sample prompts - due 2027-12-10
Samantha Ortiz - share internal compliance checklist and list of allowed IP ranges - due 2027-12-07
Dana Kim - confirm pilot dataset and success criteria (latency, accuracy, multilingual coverage) - due 2027-12-09
next_steps: Send security & compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, SAML/KMS notes)
Share draft SOW for 8-week Dedicated pilot with 32k context models
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Kim (Vectora CTO), Marcus Li (Vectora ML Eng), Samantha Ortiz (Vectora Infra)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick around-robin, i'm alex from redwood, ae on the account. priya is our se and will do most of the model/bench talk. dana, wanna kick us off with a little about vectora and what you're trying to solve?

[00:12] Dana: yeah, thanks alex. we've been building a doc-intelligence product for enterprise customers, lots of multi-ling contracts, technical manuals. primary asks: long context ingest (we're seeing docs up to 200k chars so ~30k+ tokens), multilingual (english, japanese, spanish, french), and ability to call our internal search/ksys? sorry, k-sys, uh internal db via function call. security is big - some customers require on-prem or VPC & customer-managed keys.

[00:34] Marcus: and from ml side, we care about quality vs cost tradeoffs. prefer open models where possible, but need tool-calling and structured output support. we also want to understand latency at 50 concurrent users.

[00:48] Priya: great, that's helpful. to frame the convo: we'll go through model options we commonly recommend for long context and multilingual, then deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and then talk tooling - function calling, RAG patterns and benchmarks.

[01:10] Alex: quick note - some of our customers prefer hosted to try things out, then move to dedicated for predictable throughput, and private for regulated customers. we'll cover those tradeoffs.

[01:25] Dana: perfect. priya, curious on open models - we've been evaluating llama2-70b, mistral 1.2, and falcon-180b-ish variants. any strong recommendations?

[01:36] Priya: sure. high level: Llama-family (llama2 or llama3 community forks) often have good instruction-following but context length and tokenization vary. Mistral and Mistral-instruct are strong at 8k/32k variants; some vendors offer 64k context extensions. Falcon-180b historically has good generative quality but needs tuned quant and kernel work for perf. We also see hybrid approaches: use a smaller, cheaper 8k model for routing/intent + a 32k long-context model for final syntheses.

[02:10] Marcus: what about MPT or mosaic? we looked at MPT-30B for cost reasons.

[02:16] Priya: MPT variants are decent for some tasks, but multilingual and instruction-heavy behaviors can lag compared to Mistral/Llama derivatives. for translation or strong multilingual retrieval, you might look at models that were pre-trained multilingual or have good fine-tune instruction sets. also consider quantization - 4-bit quant can save $$$ but needs quality testing.

[02:42] Samantha: on deployment, if we pick dedicated, do we still get function-calling support and same api? our security folks want to confirm feature parity.

[02:51] Alex: yes - feature parity is a goal. dedicated gives reserved capacity and data isolation; private gives you customer-managed control plane and network, plus kms integration. function-calling, streaming, and embeddings all work across modes, but the runtime/kernel tuning might differ a bit in private if you're on specific hardware.

[03:12] Dana: you mentioned 64k context - is that realistic with open models? we have a subset of docs that need >32k.

[03:20] Priya: it's doable but with caveats. some model forks provide extended context via recomputation and windowing - we lean on a mix: chunk + RAG + KV cache for tokens that are reused. Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching which helps for repeated traversal, and we can patch in a 64k variant if you want to benchmark. note there are latency/cost tradeoffs as context grows.

[03:48] Marcus: approx numbers? latency expectations with 32k context on a 70b-ish model?

[03:53] Priya: ballpark - on dedicated A100/V100-equivalent, tail latencies for single-stream generation could be 600-1500ms per 512 tokens depending on kernels and batching. for 32k context the encoding/atts ramp up; we typically see generation startup + attention cost scale roughly linearly, so budget for higher token compute. If you need sub-200ms p99 then you might need smaller models or more aggressive quant + distillation.

[04:28] Dana: cost is a big factor. how do we decide hosted vs dedicated vs private from a $ perspective?

[04:35] Alex: hosted is best for eval and early production - pay-as-you-go per token. Dedicated is a monthly reserved node commit - predictable but higher baseline; more cost-effective at scale. Private has licensing + infra ops costs. we'll send a cost-model comparing per-token hosted vs amortized dedicated numbers for your throughput.

[04:56] Samantha: about security - KMS integration, HSM? how does private work with our key mgmt?

[05:03] Priya: private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and brings the control plane into your VPC. audit logs and SIEM hooks are available. hosted has SOC2, private gives you on-prem or VPC options. we'll attach our SOC2 report and the integration notes.

[05:22] Marcus: function-calling - we need to call our internal search and DB. do you support structured function outputs and schema enforcement?

[05:29] Priya: yes; function/tool calling is supported. we provide typed outputs and function schemas; in practice you can route a call to an internal lambda or container. for private deployments this runs in your network. small transcription note - sometimes the autogenerated function names get munged in logs.

[05:50] Dana: localization - japanese is important, tone matters for some docs. do models need additional finetune or can we rely on base models?

[05:57] Priya: depends on dataset. some models are strong out of the box for mainstream languages; for domain-specific tone we recommend light fine-tune or instruction-tuning with in-domain prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant / fine-tune vs prompt-engineering tradeoffs.

[06:15] Alex: also wanted to call out tooling - we surface per-prompt cost, token breakdown, and tracing in console. that helps you root-cause quality regressions when you change model or quant.

[06:30] Marcus: any redwood-verified benchmarks for long-context?

[06:34] Priya: we have internal profiles and can run a custom benchmark against your sample dataset. typical plan: we run 3 models (cheapest 8k, mid 32k, and high-quality 32/64k) with sts: latency, throughput at 50 concurrent users, and quality on your eval prompts.

[06:55] Dana: what's a realistic timeline to get a pilot running?

[06:59] Alex: quick POC - 2 weeks to stand up hosted tests once you share dataset & prompts; Dedicated pilot with reserved nodes and SOW typically 4-6 weeks. Private (on-prem) is longer due to network/infra: 6-12 weeks depending on approvals.

[07:18] Samantha: for private we need an installable package or helm charts?

[07:22] Priya: we provide a private deployment bundle: helm charts, terraform snippets, runbooks, and optional on-prem appliance. we'll share the runbook.

[07:34] Alex: any blockers on your side for starting a hosted eval?

[07:37] Dana: we need legal ok on data processing, and infra needs the IP ranges. also budget sign-off.

[07:45] Alex: ok we'll send security & IP ranges + draft MSA and SOW for pilot.

[07:51] Marcus: a couple of tech clarif: does the runtime support continuous batching and memory KV for decoder-only models?

[07:58] Priya: yes we support continuous batching, KV cache management, and optimized attention kernels. for decoder-only with very long contexts we use chunked attention + caching to avoid re-encoding everything each request. some model variants need custom kernels - we handle selection automatically but for private on-prem we may ask for hardware details.

[08:20] Dana: what about model updates/rollouts? can we pin versions?

[08:24] Alex: yes, you can pin model versions and use canary/A-B rollouts via the console. Dedicated customers get priority routing and SLA options.

[08:33] Samantha: do you keep logs of prompt contents in hosted? retention policy?

[08:38] Priya: hosted has configurable retention; by default logs are retained short-term but we offer longer retention for enterprise plans. Private gives you full control of logs. we'll include the retention options in the security pack.

[08:51] Dana: anything else on multilingual inference? latency hit for translations?

[08:56] Priya: translation adds compute; using a bilingual model often costs less than call-out translation plumbing. if you do translation + understanding you'll double the token ops so plan cost accordingly. Redwood Optimize can simulate cost impact given your volume.

[09:12] Alex: recap and next steps: alex sends pricing + security pack + IP ranges; priya sends benchmark plan and sample prompts; samantha sends compliance checklist; dana confirms dataset & criteria. schedule pilot kickoff week of 12/12.

[09:30] Dana: that works. quick Q - do you have a recommended model for best balance of quality/cost for our use-case?

[09:36] Priya: preliminary: try Mistral 32k variant for multilingual long-context as baseline, Llama-derivative 70b for higher instruction fidelity if you need more specialized reasoning, and a small 8k (MPT or distilled) for routing. we'll test Falcon-180b variant if you want the highest generation qual but expect more infra tuning.

[09:57] Marcus: ok we'll prioritize Mistral + Llama test.

[10:00] Alex: great. i'll follow up with the docs this afternoon. thanks everyone.

[10:05] Dana: thanks all.

End of transcript.
